workstream: U27 -- strategy change: initialize near the known standing solution, then learn recovery around it
question: Can PPO preserve a known successful stance and learn recovery around it? (Not: can PPO rediscover walking from scratch, or repair a policy that already falls.)
motivation: U20-U26 all converged to policies that fall within 20-75 steps of a 200-step episode, regardless of reward tuning (U26) or exploration-std tuning (U23/U24). Strategy change, not another local fix: start the policy AT the known-good zero-action solution instead of hoping PPO finds its way there from a generic random init.
reporting_qualifications: U26's branch B (w_action_rate=0.3) is adopted provisionally on the strength of ONE comparison -- it has not been checked across multiple training seeds, and that has not changed in U27.

Prior claims about 'exact resumption' (U26) are amended: saving optimizer state is necessary but not sufficient for exact resumption. RNG stream position, the observation normalizer's exact update sequence, LR/entropy schedule position, and rollout-buffer/environment state also matter and were NOT all preserved in U26's resume path. U26's continuations are best understood as CLOSE, disclosed warm starts, not bit-exact resumptions, even with optimizer state restored. U27 does not resume from anything -- it is a fresh run -- so this caveat is recorded here as a correction to prior framing, not as a defect in U27 itself.

implementation.zero_mean_init: train_ppo.py ActorCritic(zero_mean_init=True): the final actor_mean Linear layer's weight AND bias are zeroed exactly (hidden layers keep ordinary orthogonal init). Verified (not assumed): actor_mean(x)==0 for arbitrary random inputs, and a full 200-step deterministic rollout through the complete observation/action/reward pipeline reproduced the zero-action baseline's return to within floating-point tolerance (193.0046 both ways) and identical step count.
implementation.exploration_std_selection: Empirical sweep (zero-mean policy, sampled actions, 15 repeats each, reset_qvel_noise_std=0): logstd=-1.5 (std=0.223) 0% full survival; -2.0 (0.135) 0%; -2.5 (0.082) 0%; -3.0 (0.050) 73.3% full survival, mean 184.2/200 steps, falls (when they occur) still last a long time (min 123 steps); -3.5 (0.030) 100% full survival (zero fall exposure -- judged too conservative, no failure signal to learn from). Chose logstd=-3.0: 'usually' upright (73%) while retaining real fall exposure, matching the instruction's 'usually,' not 'always.'
implementation.reset_perturbations: cara_env.py CaraWalkEnvConfig.reset_qvel_noise_std (default 0.0, reproduces every prior deterministic-reset result exactly -- regression-checked). When >0, adds N(0, std) noise to each of the 12 actuated joints' initial qvel inside reset(), using the already-seeded self._rng. First and only perturbation family tested this session, per instruction.

training.config: zero_mean_init=True, init_logstd=-3.0, w_action_rate=0.3 (U26's adopted value), desired_vx=0.0 fixed (no curriculum -- stage-0 only, per instruction), fresh start (no --resume-from), seed=0
training.budget: 400,000 steps, bounded and set before starting, matching U26's per-branch scale
training.eval_every: 5 iterations, deterministic-mean rollout from nominal reset -> best-by-standing-performance checkpoint saved separately from the final checkpoint
training.initial_checkpoint_saved: checkpoint_0_init.pt -- the untrained, zero-mean-init policy, saved before training started
training.result: fall_rate hit 0.0 by iteration 16 of 195 (global_step 32,768 -- 8.2% of budget) and stayed at 0.0 for essentially the entire remainder of training (two single-iteration blips to 0.05-0.1 that immediately recovered). Deterministic eval_steps hit the maximum (200) by iteration 5 (global_step 10,240 -- 2.6% of budget, 11.6s wall time) and never needed to improve further -- the best-checkpoint mechanism locked in almost immediately.
training.contrast_with_U20_U26: Every previous approach (from-scratch random init, curriculum, exploration-std reduction, reward-weight tuning) got stuck falling within 20-75 steps for its ENTIRE training budget (300k-800k steps). This run reached and held full-episode survival within the first 3% of a much smaller budget.

evaluation.checkpoint_tested: u27_seed0_best.pt (best-by-standing-performance; locked in at iteration 5, effectively identical to the final checkpoint given fall_rate stayed at 0 throughout)

1_deterministic_nominal_reset.verdict: Learning PRESERVES the standing solution -- matches the zero-action baseline exactly on this metric.

2_sampled_nominal_reset.verdict: Exploration is tolerable at this std -- correction from prior framing: this tests ACTION-SAMPLING robustness only, not robustness to initial-state variation. Contrast with U23: the ORIGINAL (non-zero-mean) untrained policy's sampled rollouts fell 100% of the time in a mean of 21.3 steps; this policy, after training, survives the full episode 80% of the time.

3_deterministic_perturbed_vs_zero_action.magnitude_selection: swept 0.5-8.0 rad/s against ZERO ACTION first: the passive position-PD baseline is fully robust (100% full-episode survival) up to ~3 rad/s and only starts degrading past 4 rad/s. Below ~4 rad/s this test cannot discriminate anything -- confirmed empirically (0.5 rad/s: 100% vs 100%, uninformative), not assumed to be 'small enough' by default. 6.0 rad/s chosen as the primary test point (zero-action ~70% survival -- enough room for a learned policy to show a real difference in either direction).
3_deterministic_perturbed_vs_zero_action.verdict: Learned policy shows a real but MODEST recovery edge over zero action -- not dramatic, but a consistent, directional signal (wins head-to-head 3x more often than it loses), not noise in either direction.

net_assessment: The strategy change worked decisively for its stated first goal: PPO preserved the known standing solution almost immediately (2.6% of budget) and held it reliably, something no from-scratch or continued-training approach achieved in 300k-800k steps across U20-U26. The recovery question (the actual new milestone) has a real but modest positive answer at this budget: a consistent, directional edge over pure passive standing under joint-velocity perturbations large enough to challenge the passive baseline itself, though nowhere near a dramatic demonstration of feedback control. Next directions, not started here: expand the SAME perturbation family's magnitude/duration range gradually (per instruction, do not add payload/friction/actuator randomization simultaneously); check reliability across additional seeds (per the explicit reporting qualification that one comparison, including this one, does not establish reliability); or extend training budget now that the destructive-early-fall problem is gone and evaluation shows meaningful headroom before the 200-step ceiling in the sampled-nominal and perturbed conditions.
